papers.title: SmartKrishi-AI: A Survey of AI-Integrated Agriculture Decision Support and Farm Resource Management
papers.authors: Namrata Shinde, Tejashree Torave, Gayatri Bhise, Suhani Yadav, Prof. P. N. Kadam
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Agricultural choices depend heavily on a complex mix of environmental variables, including soil properties, fluctuating weather patterns, crop compatibility, market dynamics, pest threats, and the availability of vital farming resources. Most contemporary digital services target only one of these factors, forcing growers to manually gather data from multiple disconnected websites and local contacts. This paper reviews recent developments related to SmartKrishi–AI, a conceptual, integrated platform designed for agricultural decision-making and asset coordination. Our analysis evaluates several vital domains, including crop recommendation frameworks, weather forecasting networks, commodity price models, plant disease diagnostics, public welfare discovery, equipment leasing, and labor scheduling. We analyze recent research from 2023 to 2026 indexed across major venues such as IEEE, Elsevier/ScienceDirect, and MDPI, exploring their mathematical approaches, dataset constraints, evaluation methods, and practical challenges. papers.title: From spectral signatures to LiDAR-based moisture monitoring: a machine learning-based framework
papers.authors: Parham Jafary, Kourosh Zareinia, Lesley G. Campbell, Habiba Bougherara
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Intelligent Robotics and Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Early, non-invasive detection of moisture deficits in soilless substrates is essential for precision irrigation and condition monitoring in controlled-environment agriculture. However, widely used substrates such as rockwool remain under-characterized spectrally, while existing sensing approaches are often contact-based or limited to laboratory conditions. This study presents a laboratory-to-robotic-deployment framework for non-contact estimation of volumetric water content (VWC) in horticultural rockwool. High-resolution UV–Vis–NIR spectroscopy spanning 200–2500 nm was first used to characterize moisture-dependent reflectance across eleven VWC levels. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) was developed for full-spectrum classification. A material-optimized rockwool water index (RWI) was then derived by identifying the wavelength triplet that maximized classification performance. Further, a multi-learner spectral drought (MLSD) model was developed and optimized for reduced-feature classification, improving the baseline class-average F1-score by 15.9% and achieving precision above 97% for nine VWC levels. papers.title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
papers.authors: Mingzhu Du, Joao Ricardo Pereira Valente, Coby van Dooremalen, Cao Zhen, Jiwen Huang
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. papers.title: An Integrated Deep Learning and Sparse Representation Framework for Apple Leaf Disease Recognition
papers.authors: Rahul Neware, Shashi Dahiya, Sudeep Marwaha
papers.abstract: Abstract Proper identification of apple leaf diseases is an important issue towards safeguarding crop production as well as the management sustainability of orchards. Manual diagnosis is widely used but is not efficient, is subjective, and cannot easily support large-scale monitoring. This paper presents a Hybrid Deep Learning and Sparse Classification Framework, which combines YOLOv8-based deep feature extraction with L1-regularized machine learning models to achieve efficient and interpretable disease recognition. A dataset of 4,006 high-resolution apple leaf images covering 9 classes Alternaria leaf spot, Brown spot, Frogeye leaf spot, gray spot, Healthy, Mosaic, Powdery mildew, Rust, and Scab was used. After 60 epochs, YOLOv8 attained a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 98.10% at IoU 0.5, a precision of 95.16%, and a recall of 95.97%. The resulting 3,648-dimensional feature space was narrowed down to 319 dimensions using Lasso feature selection, achieving 13.48% sparsity without losing important discriminatory information. papers.title: TaxoAttention: fusing semantic and hierarchical taxonomic models with attention-guided augmentation for mosquito identification
papers.authors: Sameerah Talafha, Thomas Jenkins, Atharva Mhaskar, Roy Faiman, Autumn Goodwin
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level identification of mosquitoes remains a critical bottleneck in vector surveillance, particularly when dealing with morphologically similar taxa or field-damaged specimens. In this study, we introduce a deep learning framework that integrates hierarchical taxonomic structure with attention-based feature learning to improve classification performance under real-world imaging conditions. The model combines a semi-fixed, taxonomy-informed feature stream with a fully trainable semantic stream. It further employs dynamic attention-guided augmentation, designed to focus training on diagnostically relevant regions, such as wing venation, tarsal banding, and palpal morphology, and to reduce the influence of the background. Evaluated on a standardized, predominantly field-collected dataset (MosquitoTax-200) representing 32 species across Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex with 200 images per species, our approach achieves 84.6% macro-averaged precision (mAP), 5.0 percentage points above an Xception baseline trained with standard cross-entropy loss and used as a control. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. papers.title: Dynamic spatio-temporal sequential ordinal models: Application to invasive weeds
papers.authors: Geoffrey R. Hosack, Wen‐Hsi Yang, Kyana N. Pike, Luke S. O’Loughlin, Emma Cook
papers.source: OpenAlex / Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract The multivariate sequential ordinal model is investigated for use in the Bayesian analysis of spatio-temporal ordinal data. The sequential ordinal model likelihood is equivalent to a binary model conditional on unknown regression coefficients and spatio-temporal random effects. Therefore estimation and prediction in the space-time context can proceed using the well-established dynamic generalised linear model framework. Moreover, the sequential ordinal model avoids the ordering constraints on the threshold parameters that determine the category break points required by cumulative ordinal models, and so simplifies the estimation procedure for high-dimensional space-time applications using Bayesian inference. The dynamic spatio-temporal sequential ordinal model is applied to estimate the cover-abundance of four invasive alien weed species. These weeds are observed by means of a modified Braun-Blanquet score that is commonly used in vegetation studies and constitutes ordinal data. papers.title: A unified YOLOv11 framework for multi-crop detection of diseases, pests and nutrient deficiencies, with preliminary field validation and mobile decision support
papers.authors: Hajar Hamdaoui, Hind Mesbah, Mashail Nasser Alzain, Yassine Zarrouk, Hanae Al Kaddouri
papers.abstract: Diseases, insect pests and nutrient deficiencies account for substantial annual crop losses worldwide, yet field diagnosis remains largely dependent on expert visual inspection. Although deep learning has shown considerable promise, most existing studies focus on a single crop or stress category under controlled conditions, with limited attention to nutrient deficiencies and few progressing to real-world deployment. This study presents a unified crop-stress detection framework covering 53 classes (41 biotic stresses, five nutrient deficiencies and seven healthy classes) across seven economically important crops of the Oriental region of Morocco. A dual-device dataset of 159,000 images was assembled, 90.4% acquired in the field with a DSLR camera and a smartphone and 9.6% from open-access sources used for training only. A lightweight YOLOv11n detector was trained at 832 × 832 resolution, with all settings selected on a separate field-acquired validation partition. On an independent test partition not used for model selection, it achieved Precision = 0.977, Recall = 0.972, F1-score = 0.974, mAP@50 = 0.975 (95% CI 0.973–0.977) and mAP@50–95 = 0.953, outperforming YOLOv8n trained under

papers.title: Beneath the surface: a survey evaluating ASF preparedness across the Caribbean and Latin America
papers.authors: Rachael Schulte, Michelle L. Schultze, Guillermo Arcega Castillo, Luis Pablo Hervé-Claude, Emilio Arnaldo León
papers.abstract: Abstract African swine fever (ASF) threatens pig production across the Americas, yet empirical data on preparedness capacity remain sparse. To inform regional planning and capacity building, we conducted a comparative assessment of ASF preparedness across countries and territories (hereafter “territories”) in the Caribbean basin. The final sample size was 18 territories, 41% of the 44 territories identified as the target population in and around the Caribbean basin. Via semi-structured interviews, respondents completed a 0–10 agreement-scale questionnaire investigating ASF preparedness. Quantitative analysis was used to construct a territory-by-statement matrix and Spearman correlation matrix. Qualitative data were analyzed inductively. A wide range of preparedness scores were found, with the highest preparedness score observed for the presence of legislative authority to prevent and respond to ASF incursion, and the lowest score observed for the characterization of the feral swine population. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. The Potential Ecological Risk (PER) index showed high and very high risk for the elements. For all elements, the Hazard Index (HI) values were higher for children than for adults. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Predicting termite risk to North Korean wooden architectural heritage using climate data
papers.authors: Sihyun Kim, Jisoo Kim
papers.abstract: Termite damage to wooden architectural heritage is a growing concern under climate change, yet no assessment exists for North Korea, where field survey is currently impractical. Framed within the hazard-exposure-vulnerability paradigm of heritage risk assessment, we integrated climate data, GIS-based spatial analysis, a biological model of termite-driven wood decay, and regression analysis to assess risk to 67 heritage sites. Termites can potentially inhabit 62.1% of the land area, and 64 sites (95.5%) fall within this range, with an estimated above-ground activity period of 195.2 days. Using the Relative Termite Damage Potential Index and Jenks natural breaks, habitable sites were classified as 15 low-, 32 moderate- and 17 high-risk, and every World Heritage component in the country fell in the high-risk class. Regression on location explained 86.4% of the variance, risk increasing toward lower latitudes. This first assessment offers a transferable risk-assessment framework for heritage in regions with poor access.

papers.title: Morphological and Spatial Characteristics of Indian Pangolin (Manis crassicaudata) Burrows in the Protected Semi-Arid Landscape of Saurashtra, Gujarat, India
papers.authors: Sandeep Kumar Kaushal, Ahmad Masood Khan
papers.abstract: Abstract The Indian Pangolin ( Manis crassicaudata ) is classified as endangered and is an important ecosystem engineer of the ecosystem where it exists; however, there are very few quantitative baseline studies that evaluate its burrow characteristics and habitat selection. This longitudinal study spanned 2024–2026 and included two different types of natural protected areas located in Saurashtra, Gujarat, India: the basaltic Barda Wildlife Sanctuary and alluvial Mitiyala Wildlife Sanctuary. Using Average Nearest Neighbour analysis, we identified evidence of significant clustering for both feeding burrows (Z = -13.76; P < 0.001 in Barda; Z = -9.72; p < 0.001 in Mitiyala) and resting burrows (Z = -3.99; p < 0.001 in Barda; Z = -3.39; p < 0.001 in Mitiyala). Using the proximity of commute distances, we calculated an average foraging commute of 331.03 ± 360.59 m in Mitiyala, suggesting that the pangolin spatially separates locations used for feeding versus resting, likely to reduce the risk of predation. Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus and Pepino Mosaic Virus Differentially Modulate Disease Severity of Bacterial Pith Necrosis and Bacterial Canker in Tomato
papers.authors: Evanson Ngugi, Ilana Bekelman, Nir Berholz, Lior Avraham, Sigal Perets
papers.abstract: Worldwide tomato production is increasingly challenged by complex disease outbreaks involving multiple interacting pathogens. In Israel, recent years have seen a marked rise in vascular collapse symptoms in greenhouse-grown tomatoes, coinciding with the widespread emergence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) and pepino mosaic virus (PepMV). Here, we investigated the bacterial and viral agents associated with these outbreaks and examined how viral infection influences the development and severity of bacterial diseases that cause vascular collapse. Surveys conducted between 2021 and 2026 revealed that tomato pith necrosis outbreaks were associated with a diverse bacterial community dominated by members of the Pseudomonadales and Enterobacterales , while bacterial canker outbreaks were exclusively linked to Clavibacter michiganensis . Multilocus sequence analysis showed that pith necrosis–associated Pseudomonas isolates clustered primarily within the P. syringae , and P. corrugata phylogroups. papers.title: Advanced biomedical materials and drug delivery systems for gastrointestinal applications: current understanding and future perspectives
papers.authors: Yijie Hu, Shengjie Luo, Zixin Chen, Rongkang Huang, Feng Wang
papers.abstract: The gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a major site of ulcerative, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. It also functions as an important interface in systemic metabolic regulation. The effectiveness of current treatments is often limited by poor drug stability and short residence times in the GI tract, insufficient exposure at the target site, and unnecessary systemic exposure. These limitations are compounded by regional pH changes, digestive enzymes, mucus turnover, peristaltic clearance, immune surveillance, and microbial metabolism. Advanced biomedical materials, including mucoadhesive hydrogels, stimuli-responsive nanoplatforms, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived scaffolds, are increasingly being developed to protect cargo, prolong mucosal residence, enable site-selective release, support tissue repair, and modulate immune or microbial processes. However, selecting a suitable material and delivery strategy for different GI diseases remains challenging. papers.title: Branch piles as microhabitats for soil mesofauna: Responses to management-created deadwood structures
papers.authors: Norbert Flórián, Veronika Gergócs, Péter Ódor, Tamás Németh, Bence Kovács
papers.abstract: Integrating structural elements such as deadwood into managed forests is increasingly recognised as an important strategy for biodiversity conservation, including soil-dwelling communities. However, the effects of management-created woody structures on non-saproxylic soil fauna, and their dependence on forest management and season, remain insufficiently understood. We investigated how branch-pile microhabitats affect soil mesofaunal density and community composition, whether these effects depend on forest-management treatment, and how they vary seasonally in an 80-year-old oak-hornbeam temperate forest. Eight years after branch-pile establishment, we compared three microhabitats: beneath branch piles, immediately adjacent to them, and open litter-covered soil, across five forest-management treatments and three seasons. We assessed mesofaunal density and community composition, with Collembola examined at finer taxonomic resolution. Branch-pile microhabitats were associated with higher densities of most mesofaunal taxa across forest-management treatments, indicating consistent effects across management contexts. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. One of the principal pathological hallmarks of ALS is the abnormal cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein involved in RNA metabolism and stress granule dynamics. Mutations in the TARDBP gene have been associated with both familial and sporadic ALS and are thought to contribute to altered cellular stress responses, defective RNA processing, and impaired proteostasis. papers.title: Modeling associations between migratory movements and seasonal honey bee colony survival: a machine-learning approach with big data
papers.authors: Nico Coallier, Maxime Fraser Franco, Ryan William Kuesel, Brandon Kingsley Hopkins
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of commercial beekeeping practices, specifically colony movement and co-variates, on honeybee colony survival. We used data on 362,884 colonies from 62 beekeepers over 4 years (2022-2026) to compare the numberof times a given hive was moved to the survival or death of those hives. We found that excessive transportation significantlyreduces the probability of surviving beyond one season. We also found a positive effect between the predicted longevity andthe average days between moves, suggesting movement strategy could mitigate the negative impact of movements on longevity.Finally, we’ve compared 3 machine learning survival models and their combination on C-index and Brier score. We’ve thenselected the best model and data format for the features importance and simulation. We generated 15 different movementsscenarios on 3 simulated beekeeping seasons. The results of our model comparison highlight the importance of a proper datastructure to achieve optimal performance on censored data.

papers.title: Antimicrobial cetylpyridinium chloride disrupts the mitochondrial electron transport chain with potency comparable to cyanide, via cardiolipin interference at cytochrome c
papers.authors: Emily L. Ledue, Noah E. Adelman, Madeleine K. Lorenger, Dylan J. Wagner, Sophie K. Trafton
papers.abstract: Abstract People are widely exposed to the antimicrobial cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) via consumer products, but CPC is a mitochondrial toxicant with potency comparable to that of canonical mitotoxicants. CPC is largely unregulated despite growing usage, bioavailability, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. Previously, we showed, in several cell types at non-cytotoxic and exposure-relevant doses, CPC inhibits ATP and oxygen consumption rate. Mitochondrial toxicity is linked to multiple diseases, but CPC has not been studied epidemiologically, and its mode of action is unknown. To determine why oxygen consumption is hampered by CPC, we hypothesized that CPC inhibits electron transport chain components, cardiolipin, or Krebs cycle enzymes. Here, we show that, in primary human skin cells, an immune mast cell model, and isolated mitochondria, CPC apparently inhibits multiple electron transport chain Complexes. Detailed investigation pinpointed the mechanism to the distal end of electron transport chain: Complex III-cytochrome c-Complex IV. papers.authors: Ana Paula Ferreira, Bruno Vinícius Daquila, Elton Luiz Scudeler, Natieli Jenifer Mateus-Corniani, Caroline Fetzner
papers.abstract: Abstract Metarhizium anisopliae is widely used in biological control programs against insect pests, although information on its compatibility with natural enemies remains limited. This study evaluated the selectivity of M. anisopliae isolate IBCB 425 (Hypocreales: Clavicipitaceae) toward the predatory lacewings Ceraeochrysa cincta (Schneider, 1851) and Chrysoperla externa (Hagen, 1861) (Neuroptera: Chrysopidae). Larvae of both species were fed Diatraea saccharalis (Fabricius, 1794) (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) eggs treated with 4 × 10 7 , 8 × 10 7 , or 4 × 10 8 conidia/mL until the prepupal stage. Larval mortality, pupal, adult, and egg inviability, oviposition, and midgut morphology were evaluated using statistical, histological, and ultrastructural analyses. Under the experimental conditions, exposure to M. anisopliae did not cause detectable adverse effects. Larval mortality ranged from 4 to 8% in C. cincta and from 6 to 8% in C. externa . Pupal inviability ranged from 2 to 6% in both species, whereas adult inviability ranged from 6 to 8% in C. cincta and from 4 to 6% in C. externa . papers.abstract: Rice leaf disease is of important concern in developing countries, especially when the livelihood of a major population is dependent on agronomy. Rice is considered a staple crop in South Asian countries, foliar pathogens in rice cause substantial yield loss and economical burden. This review systematically examines the evolution of machine learning and state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for the detection of rice leaf disease. Unlike studies concentrated only on model performance, this review focused on the complete pipeline - spanning challenges observed during image acquisition, preprocessing steps, data characterization, features representation, classification methodology used, along with misused evaluation metrics leading to unsuccessful real-world deployment. This literature reveals a clear paradigm shift from handcrafted feature-based machine learning systems to deep learning architectures, because of their consistently high accuracy, learning discriminative representations directly from raw images without any human intervention. papers.title: Impact of Climate Change on Agricultural Resources in Kenya: A Review Paper
papers.authors: Daniel Kiangi Munyao, Carolyne Cherotich Rono, Joash Keino Kibett
papers.source: OpenAlex / East African Journal of Agriculture and Biotechnology
papers.abstract: Agriculture is inherently dependent on weather and climate, relying on land, water, and other natural resources that are increasingly affected by changing climatic patterns. In Kenya, where agriculture contributes approximately 25% to GDP and employs 40% of the population, understanding these impacts is critical for food security and economic stability. This review paper synthesises existing literature from 2000 to 2026 to examine the impact of climate change on agricultural resources in Kenya. A systematic review of peer-reviewed articles, reports, and grey literature was conducted using Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Springer, and ResearchGate. The findings indicate that climate change has significantly affected Kenya's agricultural resources through: (1) altered water availability, including drought, reduced lake volumes, and flooding; (2) soil degradation through erosion, nutrient loss, and reduced microbial activity; (3) increased pest and disease incidence affecting crops and livestock; (4) declining crop productivity due to heat stress and erratic rainfall; and (5) mass livestock deaths from prolonged drought. papers.authors: Xin Liu, Yilin Gu, Qingxia Kong, Hongyue Dang
papers.abstract: The increasing global antibiotic resistance has created a pressing need for new antimicrobial drugs. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) come into the spotlight for their antibacterial properties, particularly against multidrug-resistant pathogens. Because AMPs typically mediate localized interference competition, we hypothesize that spatially confined, highly competitive microbiomes create ecological conditions that favor the evolution, expression, and diversification of AMPs, although spatial structure may equally promote niche partitioning, cooperative interactions, and producer–resistant coexistence. We therefore propose, as a working hypothesis, that marine particles represent promising yet underexplored reservoirs of untapped marine AMPs. Marine particles are ubiquitous throughout the ocean, ranging from the sunlit surface waters to the deepest hadal environments. They are densely colonized microhabitats where nutrient gradients, spatial proximity, chemical signaling, and interspecies competition among microorganisms converge—unique characteristics that position marine particles as natural laboratories for the evolution of novel AMPs. papers.abstract: Abstract The introduction of invasive plant species has become a major threat to the unique biodiversity and ecological integrity of the Galápagos Islands. One of the most aggressive invaders is Syzygium jambos (Myrtaceae), which forms dense tree stands that suppress native vegetation and alter ecosystem functioning. Remarkably, populations of this invasive rose apple tree have undergone a pronounced decline on San Cristóbal Island in recent years. In this study, we combined remote sensing with pathogen identification to investigate this phenomenon. Spectral and spatial analyses revealed an approximate 73% reduction in S. jambos tree cover between 2018 and 2024. Concurrently, symptomatic leaves were examined using morphological characterization and molecular diagnostics. Nested PCR amplification followed by internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region sequencing confirmed the presence of Austropuccinia psidii , a myrtle rust fungus known to infect members of the Myrtaceae family, in symptomatic S. jambos leaves. papers.abstract: Abstract Top pruning is an effective way to produce "orchard-style" forest seed orchards, and phosphorus (P) fertilization can improve the reproductive ability of Masson pine (Pinus massoniana) to some extent. However, it is necessary to determine the absorption and distribution of carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) nutrients by applying phosphorus fertilizer under top pruning. Overall, top pruning promoted female cone formation in high-yielding P. massoniana clones and significantly affected the downward movement of the fruiting layer, the density of female cones in the lower branches increased by 25.45%~64.97% after top pruning. papers.title: Translating pathogen biology into diagnostic and management strategies for gummy stem blight in cucumber production
papers.authors: Aastha Ranjan, A.D Lu, Charles Hutton, Oscar Bricknell, Andrew Redman
papers.abstract: Gummy stem blight (GSB) is a major disease of cucurbits caused by Stagonosporopsis spp. and is increasingly problematic in intensive cucumber production systems, particularly where warm, humid environments favour infection, sporulation and rapid disease spread. GSB can infect vegetative and reproductive tissues and remain latent in fruit for several days before visible symptoms develop, creating a distinctive commercial challenge: disease may be difficult to detect before harvest yet cause significant post-harvest losses, reducing grower and retailer confidence. Compounding these problems, current diagnostic tools for detecting pre-symptomatic infection are often insufficiently validated for species specificity, sensitivity, turnaround time, cost, crude-sample compatibility and practical use by production staff. Many of these limitations reflect the relative lack of genomic resources for Stagonosporopsis. Therefore, this review integrates evidence from other pathosystems with current knowledge of Stagonosporopsis taxonomy, infection biology, epidemiology, diagnostics, fungicide resistance, effector biology and host resistance to identify pathways towards grower-ready tools. papers.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. papers.abstract: Abstract Medicinal plants are valuable sources of phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides and essential oils. Phytochemicals extracted from medicinal plants find application in different biological systems due to their varied biological activities. Rising environmental concerns along with requirement for sustainable substitutes have gained interest in multifunctional compounds from plants. Plants possess phytochemicals with antioxidant, antimicrobial and corrosion inhibition potential which make them applicable in pharmaceutical industries, food processing, environmental and industrial applications. Antioxidant potential involves free radical scavenging activity, metal chelating ability and regulation of redox reaction. Antimicrobial activity is due to alteration of the microbial cell membrane structure, enzyme inhibition and binding with microbial DNA. Corrosion inhibition potentials involve adsorption of bioactive compounds present in plants on metal surface and forming a protective layer over metal surface that reduces metal dissolution in acidic corrosive media. papers.title: Global disparities in dengue, climate, and extreme weather research: a bibliometric analysis of alignment with disease burden and climate-driven vector suitability
papers.authors: Chunyue Ai, Yi Teng, Guangju Mo, Wenyu Wang, Meshack Kipkogei Biwott
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease that imposes a substantial public health burden in tropical and subtropical regions. Temperature, rainfall, and extreme weather can affect mosquito ecology, human exposure, and the environmental suitability for transmission. This study characterized the global research landscape of dengue and extreme weather and examined whether country-level research output corresponded to dengue burden and climate-driven vector suitability. METHODS: The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 22 May 2026. Publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, authors, co-cited references, citation bursts, keyword patterns, and thematic evolution were examined using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package. Country-level publication output was linked to estimates from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 dataset, the socio-demographic index for 2021, and mean index-p values for 1990-2022. Associations between publication output and dengue burden were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation among countries classified as dengue-endemic. RESULTS: A total of 290 publications from 2008 to 2026 met the eligibility criteria.

papers.abstract: Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58, the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. AIY-specific overexpression of nlp-58 is sufficient to reproduce the thermotaxis defect, identifying AIY as an important site of NLP-58-dependent behavioral modulation. Genetic analyses further demonstrated that the thermotaxis behavior is mediated primarily through the tachykinin receptor TKR-1, the homolog of mammalian tachykinin 3 receptor (NK3R), acting in ASG and/or ASJ sensory neurons.
